hypothesis: When Coinbase USD spot trades unusually rich (cheap) relative to Binance's USDT market during US hours, after removing USDT/USD and the perp basis, the next 24h of the Binance perp drifts up (down). Trading the sign of that US-hours gap, measured against its own trailing level, beats side-matched random twins on the same entries and brackets.
mechanism: Cross-venue price gaps reflect each venue's own signed order flow, and arbitrage capital is slow, so gaps persist (Makarov & Schoar 2020). A US-session Coinbase premium marks net US spot buying (retail, institutions, after 2024-01 ETF creations routed through Coinbase Prime) that is not yet fully absorbed offshore. If that demand is persistent over hours to days (flows are autocorrelated), price continues in its direction over the next day. This is a slow flow-persistence claim at a daily horizon, not a minute-level price-discovery claim.

sources.summary: Makarov & Schoar (2020, JFE 135(2) 293-319): large, recurrent cross-exchange price deviations that often persist for weeks; they open up during large BTC appreciations; the idiosyncratic component of each exchange's signed volume explains the size of the spreads, while the common component explains most of returns. Evidence is contemporaneous, not predictive.

Alexander & Heck (2020, J. Financial Stability 50, 100776): at the minute level, unregulated perps/futures (Huobi, OKEx, BitMEX) lead price discovery; US spot exchanges and CME react rather than lead. EVIDENCE AGAINST a fast Coinbase-leads mechanism; K1 therefore claims only daily-horizon flow persistence.

CryptoQuant Coinbase Premium Index (Coinbase BTC-USD vs Binance BTC-USDT): vendor claim that sustained positive premiums 'frequently preceded or accompanied' rallies. Anecdotal, untested; motivates the direction only.

Seo, Koo & Yang (2024, Economic Modelling 135): the Kimchi premium mean-reverts only when large (threshold arbitrage), random-walk-like inside a band. Supports measuring the gap against its own trailing level, and warns that small gaps are noise.

prior: Weak. No peer-reviewed test of the premium predicting returns was found, and the price-discovery evidence points the other way at short horizons. Expect FAIL; run because the data is new to this repo and cheap.
closed_ideas_check: Not on research_loop/CLOSED_IDEAS.md and not C1/C3/C5/C6. Differs from C2 (funding fade): the perp-vs-index basis (the funding driver) is removed explicitly, the comparison is spot-vs-spot across venues and currencies, and the trade is continuation, not a fade. Differs from C4 (US-open range breakout): no price range, decision at the US close from a cross-venue gap. No crypto rows in data_spend_ledger.json for these families.
data_choice: Option (a), chosen before any data was looked at: USDT-adjusted only. Coinbase USDT-USD starts 2021-05-04, so signals exist only from then (plus 40 trading days of history). Train is about 2021-07 -> 2024-06 for BTC and ETH. No unadjusted pre-2021-05 sub-period (2020 USDT deviations of 1-2% are the size of the signal). SOL is not run as a signal source (Coinbase SOL-USD was not fetched); SOLUSDT rows will show 0 trades.

rules.instruments: BTCUSDT uses Coinbase BTC-USD; ETHUSDT uses Coinbase ETH-USD; both use Coinbase USDT-USD. Other symbols: no signals.
rules.sample: For each Coinbase 5m bar stamped t (usable at t+300), with t in [09:30, 16:00) ET on a NY weekday: g_t = ln(CB close) - ln(Binance perp 1m close of the bar opening at t+240) - ln(USDT-USD 5m close stamped t) - ln(1 + Binance premium-index 1m close of the bar opening at t+240). All four prices refer to t+300. Drop a sample if any input is missing, the USDT-USD row is not the bar stamped t, or the Binance bar is stale (zero-volume padding).
rules.daily_gap: G_d = mean of g_t over the day's samples, in bp; the day counts only with >= min_samples (70 of 78) samples.
rules.z: z_d = (G_d - mean(G over the previous lookback_days valid days)) / std(same), needing >= min_hist valid prior days. Today's G_d joins the history only after it is used.
rules.signal: decided at the close of the 1m bar opening 15:59 ET (decision time 16:00 ET, all samples available); if |z_d| >= z: side = sign(z_d).
rules.bracket: market entry at the next 1m open (engine). Stop distance = max(stop_atr * daily ATR(14) of the last completed UTC day, min_stop_pct % of the decision close). No target.
rules.exit: time exit hold_h hours after entry (end_by_time), unless stopped first. Mirror-flat book: at most one position; a signal while the mirrors are busy is skipped.
rules.warmup: WARMUP_DAYS = 90 (validation needs the trailing history; train has no data before 2021-05 anyway).

walk_forward: fixed: no parameter is selected. Both z values are judged by the frozen train gate (BTC and ETH both must pass). Any config that passes goes to validation; K counts candidates sent.
expected_trades: about 790 NY weekdays in 2021-07 -> 2024-06 per asset; |z| >= 0.5 fires on roughly 60% (~450 trades), |z| >= 1.0 on roughly 30% (~240), both above the 200-trade floor. Unknown before running.
costs_note: Median stop expected ~3% (BTC) to ~4% (ETH) from ATR(14), floor 1.5%. At a 3% stop, notional is about $16.7K: 7.6 bp round trip = $12.7 plus 1 day of swap at 3 bp = $5, about 0.035R. At the 1.5% floor, about 0.07R. Stated before running.
report_not_gate: net R by year and pre-2024-01 vs post (ETF regime change); long share; result with the 2022 bear year removed; stop vs time exits.
rejection_evidence: Reject if the frozen train gate fails for both z (any of: < 200 trades, twin p >= 0.005, net R <= 0, session CI low <= 0, stress R <= 0, a year > 40% of net R, net R <= 0 without the top 5, median stop < 1.5%, EV <= twins' EV, truncation mismatch) on BTC or ETH. Count against it (report): a pass driven by one side only, or by 2021 alone.
